liquidity.slippage_bps_basis: PRICE IMPACT against this venue's own smallest quoted rung, which EXCLUDES that rung's own spread — it is not the holder's all-in cost. The all-in figure is fill_ratio (output_usd / size). Impact is measured this way deliberately, so peg discount and source lag do not leak into it.

liquidity.two_pct_depth_basis: A FLOOR, not a measurement. The deepest rung quoted ($100,000) still clears inside 200bps, so the crossing is somewhere above where we look. Publishing it as '2% depth' would read as a limit we found. SLIPPAGE CONVENTION: TOTAL over the fill (not marginal impact at the margin), measured against this venue's own smallest quoted rung. ⚠️ That reference EXCLUDES the smallest rung's own spread, so the figure is price impact and NOT the holder's all-in cost — which is fill_ratio (output_usd / size). Both are real and they answer different questions. The same ladder classifies differently under total vs marginal and under impact vs all-in, so both halves are stated for cross-producer comparison.

depth_50bps.basis: A FLOOR, not a measurement. The deepest rung quoted ($100,000) still clears inside 50bps, so the crossing is somewhere above where we look. Publishing it as '0.5% depth' would read as a limit we found. SLIPPAGE CONVENTION: TOTAL over the fill (not marginal impact at the margin), measured against this venue's own smallest quoted rung. ⚠️ That reference EXCLUDES the smallest rung's own spread, so the figure is price impact and NOT the holder's all-in cost — which is fill_ratio (output_usd / size). Both are real and they answer different questions. The same ladder classifies differently under total vs marginal and under impact vs all-in, so both halves are stated for cross-producer comparison.

exit_mark.slippage_bps_basis: ALL-IN COST against notional: (output_usd - size) / size. Includes the venue's base spread, so it is not comparable rung-for-rung with a price-impact figure measured against a venue's own spot rung.

backing.collateral_ratio_basis: Issuer-attested collateralization, published unchanged. NETTED ON BOTH SIDES: (reserves - POL - inventory) / (supply - POL - inventory), the basis apyx switched to on 2026-06-08. POL is protocol-owned liquidity and Inventory is a net-zero bucket, so both are removed from backing and from supply rather than counted as either. ⚠️ NOT comparable to a gross collateral ratio: the generic axis cutoffs assume gross, so a netted figure sits lower for the same underlying coverage. We verify the identity independently — residual tolerance 0.01pp — rather than trusting the attested number on its own; see asset_specific.backing_attestation.attested_basis_residual_pp. ⚠️ Netting makes this asset look WORSE, not better: gross is 99.20% against the netted 98.86%, -0.34pp. Do not read a netted basis as issuer-flattering.
backing.axis_rating_basis: Rated on the generic band deliberately — no anchor exists in this analyzer, and the apparent agreement between the axis (2/5) and the published backing score (2.0/10) is COINCIDENTAL. The axis rates coverage; the score rates basket composition (~74% STRC) and dislocation, which a collateral ratio cannot express. Expect them to diverge when STRC moves without the CR moving — that is the design, not a defect.
backing.surplus_deficit_basis: GROSS reserves minus GROSS supply — not netted, unlike collateral_ratio. ⚠️ B/(B - surplus_deficit) therefore recovers 99.22%, not the published 98.88%; the two fields are not coherent on one denominator. Use collateral_ratio for coverage and this only for the absolute gross gap.
